title: A scalable platform to discover and characterize substrates of molecular glue degraders - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Researchers built an MGD discovery pipeline combining experimental and computational screening to map cereblon (CRBN)-molecular glue degrader neo-substrates and the structural rules that govern which proteins get degraded, addressing the field's reliance on serendipitous discovery.

insights.claim: Molecular glue degrader (MGD) discovery is largely serendipitous, and the specificity of MGD-mediated target selection remains poorly understood.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A systematic discovery platform could de-risk a drug class that today advances by luck, expanding the druggable proteome.
insights.quote: MGD discovery is largely serendipitous, and the specificity of MGD-mediated target selection remains poorly understood.

insights.claim: Molecular glue degraders induce degradation of non-native protein substrates (neo-substrates) through the E3 ubiquitin ligase CRL4CRBN.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cereblon remains the central hub for glue-based degradation, so mapping its interactome defines the addressable target space.

insights.claim: The team developed an MGD discovery pipeline that integrates experimental and computational screening to identify cereblon-MGD neo-substrates and the structural determinants of MGD-mediated degradation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Pairing wet-lab screens with ML prediction is the emerging template for scaling degrader target discovery.

insights.claim: The work is a summary of Galli et al.'s proteome-wide identification of the druggable CRBN interactome, positioning it as a systematic map of degradable targets.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A proteome-wide druggable CRBN map is a competitive asset for degrader-focused drug developers.
insights.quote: Proteome-wide identification of the druggable CRBN interactome.
